A fixed point can be a whole family

Toy Deutsch loop: the qubit that returns around the loop undergoes a Pauli-X flip. This is a quantum-state consistency calculation only; it does not model a spacetime path or send a signal.

ρC = ½(I + xX),   Φε(ρ) = (1−ε)XρX + εI/2

At ε = 0, every state on the X axis is fixed.

Z-basis result (0 / 1): 50% / 50%
Returned X-basis result (+ / −): 75% / 25%
Returned-state purity Tr(ρ²): 0.625
X coherence after one pass: 0.500
X coherence after 10 passes: 0.500

The classical bit rule sees only the Z-basis probabilities, so it selects 50/50. Quantum mechanics also tracks phase coherence: changing x changes X-basis statistics while leaving the state fixed under the noiseless flip. The toy replacement-noise channel selects I/2 uniquely for ε > 0, but damps X coherence by (1−ε) each pass. That is an explicit noise model, not a free CTC rule. Even a unique state is not the field's Green function, a 5D metric, or a route to an earlier event.
